    The interval part and the X-part of an object of C(D) #

    Every object M of C(D) is the direct sum of its interval part bPart M (the summands Y, A i, P i) and its X-part xPart M. The functor ρ kills the X-part, is fully faithful on objects without copies of X, and sends every object to a good representation.
